creator: Alexander Terp
description:
a_2Ky2ptlug names two directions for the shared devenv container and settles on neither. Two parallel rounds have now paid for that, and the second one found the exact mechanism.

## The mechanism, measured 2026-09-06

`devenv up` rebuilds the image with the local worktree pubkey every time, but **returns early when a container is already running**. So a container started 15 hours earlier by another worktree keeps that worktree key, and every other worktree is refused with `dev@localhost: Permission denied (publickey)`.

The script own comment in `up` predicts this failure - "a keypair generated in a second worktree produced a container that refused every login with no hint that a stale image was why" - but the guard it added covers a stale **image**, not a stale **container**. That is the gap.

`devenv down && devenv up` fixes it, and re-arms the same trap for whoever runs next.

## What two rounds cost

Round 1: the collision was avoided by hand. The integrator read a_2Ky2ptlug while scoping and told three of four slots not to touch docker at all - a whole tier removed from three slots for reasons unrelated to their work, on the strength of one person happening to have read the card.

Round 2: the one cleared slot lost time anyway, to the failure above.

So serializing by hand does not work, because the breakage is baked into a running container rather than held by a process anybody can see, and nothing checks it.

## The cheap fix, which excludes neither original direction

Compare the running container authorized key against `devenv/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` in `up`, and recreate on mismatch. That turns a confusing auth failure into a one-line recreate, and it is worth doing whichever of a_2Ky2ptlug two directions is eventually chosen.
title: The devenv key collision cost a second round, and the decision is still open
